title: Show-vs-Tell Prose Sample Pair: Parr's "Characters Show Themselves" Experiment
purpose: A paired prose experiment derived from Louisa Parr's advice in "A Story to Tell" (Gutenberg 72910): characters should reveal traits through actions and talk, not explanatory digression. The pair holds the story event constant and changes only the narrative mode — expository versus action-and-dialogue-led — so a reader can compare the information yield of each approach. This operationalizes the same source (art_01M6Q8W5S3ASWTWKS200QHGFVD, revision 1) as Iris's storyboard but shifts the medium to prose, where the distinction is more directly measurable.
attribution: Louisa Parr, 'A Story to Tell,' in On the Art of Writing Fiction (Gutenberg 72910) — documented advice restated, not quoted; source art_01M6Q8W5S3ASWTWKS200QHGFVD revision 1
